thought.text: The services use the OpenAI client (chat completions + embeddings). I'll create a small local OpenAI-compatible server accepting any model name. Let me check download progress first:

reasoning_content:
The services use the OpenAI Python client with chat.completions and embeddings. For the local endpoint, I'll implement the following:
- `GET /v1/models`
- `POST /v1/chat/completions` (non-streaming + streaming)
- `POST /v1/embeddings` (1024 dimensions)

Model names to accept: self-hosted/gpt-oss-120b, self-hosted/bge-m3, Qwen/Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507, self-hosted/gemma-4-26b-a4b-it-maas — plus whatever's in LITELLM_TEXT_MODEL etc. Since process-compose maps all model variables to the value in .env, the services will only ever request the models I put in .env. I'll set it as follows:
- LITELLM_TEXT_MODEL=self-hosted/gpt-oss-120b
- LITELLM_EMBEDDING_MODEL=self-hosted/bge-m3
- LITELLM_VISUAL_MODEL=self-hosted/gpt-oss-120b (it's a vision-capable model in reality, and the endpoint just accepts any name)

But wait — the services read model names from their own .env.local files (e.g., MODELS_SMALL_LLM=self-hosted/gemma-4-26b-a4b-it-maas). process-compose overrides LLM_MODEL, LITELLM_MODEL, LITELLM_MODEL_NAME, MODELS_LARGE_LLM, MODELS_MEDIUM_LLM, MODELS_SMALL_LLM, LLM_DB_RESEARCH_MODEL, etc., but maybe not every variable. For example, CHUNKING_MODEL is overridden. Let's accept any model name in the mock (don't validate model names). That's the simplest: accept everything, return plausible completions.

Chat responses: some modules do JSON parsing of the LLM output (document type classification, risk assessment, etc.). For installation verification, it's enough that the services start up and respond; the actual quality of the workflow execution isn't strictly required. But just to be safe, I'll make the chat endpoint return a deterministic, simple completion. Some code might expect JSON, but... at install time, it's unlikely to run a full workflow. I'll make the mock return reasonable text.

Embeddings: return 1024-dimensional vectors deterministically derived from a hash of the input (stable, non-zero). This is important for Qdrant/pgvector operations that do upserts during workflows.

Alright, let's check the progress.
